text:
alex: Quick sync — ACME POC sizing ask. They want a Private VPC deployment (single-AZ) with the ability to burst to Hosted during peak. Goal: support Q1 seasonal ramp (we're planning for ~2.5x current peak). Need: recommended pod config (GPU count/type), safety buffer, and an estimated monthly GPU-hours + cost band to share with sales.

priya: Do we have their peak RPS and model family? also any latency SLOs?

marcus: They said mix is ~60% chat (generation) / 40% embeddings. Model: community 70B variant, quantized to 4-bit. Avg input tokens ~80, avg output ~120. Peak RPS today ~25, planning for 2.5x -> ~62 RPS peak. Customer wants p99 latency <= 300ms for chat.

alex: OK — quick back-of-envelope. If a single GPU can sustain ~10 RPS for that model at p95 (with KV cache warmed), then 62 RPS -> ~6.2 GPUs active. Factor in autoscale headroom and single-AZ risk -> recommend baseline 9 GPUs and burst policy to hosted up to 14 GPUs during short peaks.

marcus: That 10 RPS/GPU number assumes batching and steady QPS. For cold-starts or if KV cache misses are higher, effective RPS drops to ~6-7. So we should add a 30% buffer for cache churn.

priya: I like making the baseline a multiple of our pod unit. Our private pod unit for that family = 4x 80GB GPUs (rackable). So baseline = 2 pods (8 GPUs) + 1 spare GPU for headroom -> 9 total as alex said. Burst to hosted for the remaining ~5 GPUs equivalent.

jen: Customer constraint: single 10Gbps transit link to our public gateway (for burst). They asked what's safe network utilization margin. They want to avoid degraded throughput if a flow hits 80% link.

alex: For embeddings heavy payloads, token IO matters. With avg tokens ~200/request, at 62 RPS that's 12.4k tokens/sec. Rough network budget: assume compressed payload ~20KB/request -> ~1.2GB/s peak which exceeds 10Gbps (1.25GB/s). So we need to either throttle embeddings parallelism or push more work to local pods. Recommend limiting burst to hosted only for chat (smaller payloads), and keep embeddings local.

marcus: Actionable config suggestion to include in sizing doc:
```
- Pod unit: 4x80GB GPUs (on-prem racks)
- Baseline: 2 pods (8 GPUs) + 1 GPU reserve -> 9 GPUs active
- Autoscale: +1 pod (4 GPUs) warm pool, plus hosted-burst policy for +5 GPU-eq on spikes
- Cache retention: 90s with sticky sessions to keep KV hit rate >= 75%
- Network: reserve 30% headroom on 10Gbps for control plane and telemetry
```

priya: For SLO math, using 9 GPUs baseline with target KV hit 75% and batching = we should meet p99 300ms for 95% of traffic, but during long sustained peaks they'd see p99 drift. Recommend an A/B canary where we monitor per-route p99 and automatically route overflow to hosted.

finance-bot: Estimated monthly GPU-hours (conservative): baseline 9 GPUs * 24 * 30 = 6480 GPU-hours. If average utilization 60% -> billable equivalent 3888 GPU-hours. With our on-prem pricing proxy ($2.20 / GPU-hour) -> $8.5k/month. If they use hosted burst ~200 GPU-hours extra / month -> +$440. (numbers rough, confirm with pricing team)

jen: Customer will need price bands. Can you include a low/med/high cost scenario? Also they asked about CAB (capacity assurance buffer) percentages — what's recommended?

alex: CAB: 20% conservative buffer for single-AZ customers. For high-risk regulated customers 30%. So for 9 GPUs baseline that means keep 2 GPUs as slack (we already have 1 reserve + expect hosted burst). Recommend we show both 20% and 30% columns in one-pager.

marcus: I'll validate model perf on a 4-GPU pod in the lab tomorrow and post concrete RPS/GPU numbers. If we can show 12 RPS/GPU with our quantized path, we can tighten recommendations.

priya: Ops checklist for the doc: network planning (10Gbps vs 25Gbps), power/rack units, warm pool sizing, monitoring (per-route p99, KV-hit, queue depth), and a fallback routing policy.

alex: TL;DR for sales: recommend "2 pod baseline (8 GPUs) + 1 spare GPU = 9 GPUs baseline; warm 1 extra pod for autoscale; host-burst up to +5 GPU-eq for short peaks; CAB 20-30%; approx 3.9k billable GPU-hrs/month -> ~$8.5k/mo (proxy)." I'll draft the one-pager and attach perf numbers after marcus' lab run. @marcus please post numbers, @jen please sync pricing asks with ACME legal. :thumbsup:

deploy-bot: Reminder: create a private-deploy-template branch for acme-poc once design doc is ready.

jen: Will do — thanks all.
